$comment: Hardware as a closed vocabulary. An adapter names a class; it never states raw numbers. Closed means schedulable, priceable and testable, and it means new hardware is a deliberate act rather than something an adapter can inflict on the fleet by accident. Locally these become docker --cpus/--memory; in the cloud they become instance types. The `lane` field routes: interactive classes run on a warm pool, batch classes get a machine that dies with the job.

nano.note: parsers, API shims, most of the catalogue

wide.note: blastn against a large database, MMseqs2

deep.note: de novo assembly, Kraken2 loading its database into RAM

local_ceiling.$comment: A workstation cannot honour `deep`. The runner clamps to these when running locally and says so, rather than failing to schedule.
